note: _qui_ (…) _et non in carbe finduciam habentes_ – who (…) and not having confidence in the flesh (Douay Version). One would expect the finite verb form _habent_ (instead of the participle plural _habentes_). – George C. Richards: _A Concise Dictionary to the Vulgate New Testament_. London 1934 (xvi, 130 pp.), p. vi, note 1.

_nostra autem conversatio in caelis est_ – our way of life is in heaven (Conte; cf. Chapter 18.1, revisions of Douay Version); unser Wandel ist im Himmel (Arndt). The Douay Version has the now obsolete “conversation” for _conversatio_. Grundl suggests “Bürgerrecht” which reflects the Greek πολίτευμα, as does _municipatus_, the word that replaces _conversatio_ in the Nova Vulgata. But “citizenship” is not what the ancient would immediately have taken as the meaning of _conversatio_.
